statements.status_notes: GO-2026-5932 is scoped to the golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package and its subpackages (openpgp/packet, openpgp/armor, openpgp/clearsign, openpgp/errors, openpgp/elgamal, openpgp/s2k), which are unmaintained and have no fixed version in any release. The only golang.org/x/crypto consumer in this image is the bundled goose binary (ClickHouse/Postgres migration tool). goose and its dependency tree do not import golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp or any of its subpackages; golang.org/x/crypto is pulled in transitively for unrelated functionality. The vulnerable openpgp code is therefore not compiled into the goose binary shipped in the image.

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package tree, which upstream has frozen with no fixed module release. The calico-node binary is built from ./cmd/calico-node/main.go at Calico v3.30.7, v3.31.6, and v3.32.1. Repository-wide search finds no golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp imports; go mod why golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp reports the main module does not need that package; go list -deps ./node/cmd/calico-node (GOOS=linux) resolves only non-openpgp x/crypto packages (for example cryptobyte, curve25519, hkdf, sha3). Go dead-code elimination therefore does not compile the vulnerable openpgp code into the shipped binary. Scout matches the golang.org/x/crypto module version against the advisory range regardless of reachability.

GO-2026-5932 covers the golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package, which upstream declares unmaintained and unsafe by design with no fixed version (all versions affected). govulncheck binary-mode symbol analysis of the shipped source-controller binary confirms vulnerable x/crypto/openpgp symbols are present and reachable (110 symbols, e.g. armor.Decode/armor.Encode), so this is not a false positive and cannot be excluded by a dependency bump. No patched x/crypto release exists and upstream fluxcd/source-controller has not migrated away from x/crypto/openpgp. Under investigation pending an upstream migration to a maintained OpenPGP implementation.
